sentences.text: According to the program, the M4 on display was pulled from a Normandy field in 1998 and restored by volunteers over eleven years. Steel treads chewed the fresh asphalt on Elm, leaving herringbone scars the city council would grumble about for weeks. Smoke from the grain elevator drifted across the studio shot all afternoon. Analysts identified the vehicles as tracked self-propelled howitzers, most likely 2S19s, moving north in groups of three. Under the stoplight an M3 half-track idled, its white star freshly stenciled over decades of repainted olive drab. Ninety-one and ramrod straight, the parade marshal refused the golf cart and walked every block of the route. Checkpoint after checkpoint, each one slower and more suspicious than the last. "Back to you in the studio — we're hearing outgoing artillery again," Marisol shouted over the rotor noise. Did you see the turret swing toward the courthouse when the crew waved at the mayor? Civilians lined the shoulder in silence; one old man raised two fingers at the passing armor, and nobody could say what he meant. Members of VFW Post 214 led the procession down Main Street, trailed by a color guard and two armored personnel carriers on loan from the museum. By dawn the correspondents had relocated to a rooftop overlooking the bridge, where engineers were laying pontoon sections under sporadic fire. At the edge of town, a boy on a bicycle races the lead vehicle for a hundred meters, then peels away laughing. "They came through at three in the morning," the baker said, still in his apron, flour on his hands. The uplink kept dropping every time the jamming trucks rolled by, so we filed the package over a landline from the hotel basement. Rain threatened all morning, but by the time the armored column reached Third Street the sun broke through above the courthouse elms. Behind the drum line, a lone bagpiper played while names were read aloud at the memorial fountain. I counted the seconds between the flash on the ridge and the thud that rattled our satellite truck: eleven. You hear the squeal of steel tracks on asphalt long before the first hull crests the overpass. "Cover your ears, honey," a father said, hoisting his daughter as the howitzer crew readied the ceremonial salute. What is the meaning of the word tank?
